items.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999
items.q: And that’s where I first heard Charlie Parker. I think he was sitting in with Milt Jackson I believe and Howard McGhee.

ctx.x: When was the first time you saw Charlie Parker play live, and what kind of effect did it have on you?

Well it’s interesting because the first music I ever played of jazz, was he gave me transcribed Benny Carter solos. And then within about a week or within that month, Ellington came to town and I saw Hodges. And Hodges played “Mood to be Wooed.” And my teacher, how wise he was, the week before I was given that for a lesson. So here I got a chance to see Hodges. And then my friend Hal Serra and I picked up the latest record of this guy called Charlie Parker and it was “KoKo.” And another record was “Shaw ‘Nuff.”…
Did he sound as good there as he did on live TV?
